newsitem.title: UK: Coffee nations decide to extend quotas.
newsitem.headline: Coffee nations decide to extend quotas.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Exporting Countries (ACPC) ended London talks with a decision to extend their coffee export quotas for one year, an official said.
The goal appeared to be to try to lock in gains from a spectacular rally in world prices if the market weakens later in the year.
Coffee nations decide to extend quotas =2

Ivory Coast Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze told reporters that details of the allocation of quotas would be decided by September. The total limit on exports for one year will be 52.75 million (60 kg) bags, the ACPC said.
The current quota accord expires on June 30 and set a total limit on exports by the 14 ACPC nations led by Brazil at 25.5 million bags for six months, so the volume limit is roughly unchanged.

This year's rally in world prices has taken them up by 80-100 percent but analysts think the market may slide later in the year, after the end of the Brazilian frost season. - - London Newsroom +44 171 542 7729
